page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-2 is an entry-level, compute-focused virtual machine instance belonging to the N1 machine family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, with a dedicated CPU allocation. The instance is equipped with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark testing, the n1-highcpu-2 demonstrates entry-level performance characteristics. Its single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is measured at 1086.39, placing it in the bottom 25%, while its multi-core CPU performance of 1408.88 falls into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block transfers registering at 13.22 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 11.3 GB/sec. Similarly, database operations and static web serving throughput rank in the lower tier of tested instances.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources rather than shared-core burstable performance. However, the low memory allocation of 2.0 GB presents a significant tradeoff, limiting its suitability for memory-intensive applications.

The n1-highcpu-2 is best suited for lightweight, CPU-bound workloads that do not require substantial memory footprints. Appropriate use cases include basic web serving, simple background workers, lightweight automation scripts, and small-scale software compilation tasks.
